Kaṅkhā, yo, mahāṭī, 3. 204. Tato(tilato)pana nikkhanto sineho telaṃ. So hi 'tilānaṃ idanti tela'nti vuccati....idañhi vacanaṃ telassa sāmaññato sinehe pavattiṃ dīpeti....api ca tela-saddoyebhuyyena tilatele vattati. Nīti, dhā. 340-1.(taဲla-saṃ)] Oil, Resin. See retangular Bracket. (1) Sesame oil. (2) Mustard oil. (3) Oil from hard tree bearing flowers which are dried and eaten and seed from which oil is extracted Madhuca longifolia. (4) Castor oil. (5) Oil from animals, (A) Bear oil. (B) Fish oil. (C) Dolphin oil. (D) Pig oil. (E) Ass or Donkey oil. (6) Oil for applying or painting. (A) Oil for applying the body. (B) Hair coat. (C) Oil for applying the foot. (D) Oil for applying wound or sore. (E) Oil for put in the shaft of the cart. Tela(na) [tela+a] (1) It is like the oil. (2) Oil Mill (Mill in which produce oil), Oil tent (mean in the tent cooking the oil as a finishing product). (Pu) (3) One who named Tela. See original.
pn: Tela. v.l. Malla. One of the ambassadors sent by Devānampiyatissa to Asoka. Mhv-ṭ.302.
